title: Germination journal
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Dissolving, separating and plants (Do All Solids Dissolve? and Allotment)
source: Seeded from science/y5 lessons 35, 36 (Germination journal (portal worksheet))
intro: To understand what a seed needs to germinate and what a plant needs to grow

questions.q: A bean in a dry, warm cupboard does not grow. Why?
questions.a: No water: seeds need water to germinate
questions.model: Check the three needs: water? No. Warmth? Yes. Air? Yes. Water is missing, so it cannot germinate.

questions.q: Which grows first: the root or the shoot?
Why does a seedling need light?
Why does the food store shrink as the seedling grows?
questions.a: The seedling uses the food for energy to grow
questions.model: Think: where does the energy come from before there are leaves? The food store. As it is used up, it shrinks.

questions.q: Look at your bean jar. Draw it, label root, shoot, seed coat, and measure the shoot in cm. Add to your journal.
questions.a: Labelled drawing with a measurement and date
questions.model: Teacher holds up a bean jar on camera and labels 'root: grows down first'.

questions.q: Plan a test to show that seeds need water to germinate.
questions.a: Two jars: damp paper and dry paper, same warmth and air; only the damp one germinates

questions.q: Why do farmers wait for spring to sow many seeds?
questions.a: Soil becomes warm enough to germinate

questions.q: Open a soaked bean, draw it and label the seed coat, food store and embryo. Then label your bean jar plant.
questions.model: Teacher draws the split bean and labels 'embryo: the baby plant'.

questions.q: Measure your bean shoot. How much has it grown since last lesson?
Why are seeds such a good food for people (beans, rice, wheat)?
questions.a: They are full of stored food for the young plant

questions.q: A seed starting to grow is...
Big question: what wakes a seed up?
The baby plant inside a seed is the...
Big question: where does a bean get its energy in the dark?
questions.a: From its food store inside the seed.
